name: sector_investment_news_sweep
what: 12-sector India-investment news sweep (one subagent per the twin's core PLI-derived sectors), replacing the earlier NewsAPI-based sweeps that were proven unreliable at scale. Every finding here was verified by opening and reading the actual source article/press release, not a search snippet. new_to_twin flags companies not already in layer 16 leads or the company DB, via the same word-boundary fragment matcher used in layers 37/41.

findings.signal: Signed a Joint Venture Cooperation Agreement with Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) on 24 Nov 2025 to incorporate a 50:50 India joint venture that will localise manufacturing, supply and maintenance of the HAMMER precision-guided air-to-ground weapon system for the Indian Air Force and Navy, targeting ~60% indigenisation over time.

Inaugurated the world's largest LEAP engine (CFM International) maintenance, repair and overhaul centre in Hyderabad, a EUR 200 million-plus investment, to reduce overseas MRO dependence for Indian carriers (IndiGo, Air India) and serve civil and military programmes; company stated it plans to triple annual revenue from Indian operations by decade end.

First defence-sector project in India approved under the 100% FDI route: Saab's plant in Jhajjar, Haryana will manufacture the Carl-Gustaf shoulder-fired weapon system (Saab's first Carl-Gustaf plant outside Sweden) for Indian forces and export, with manufacturing due to begin once the industrial licence is granted -- confirmed on record by Mats Palmberg, Saab's Chairman and Managing Director in India.

Announced a fresh Rs 100 crore investment in its Pune manufacturing facility (welding technologies, inspection equipment, precision tooling), bringing total investment at the site to Rs 510 crore over three years; the facility produces components for GE90/GEnx/GE9X and CFM LEAP commercial engines and works with 300+ local suppliers.

Developing a new Defence Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul facility in Bangalore jointly with Tata Advanced Systems, scheduled to be operational in early 2027, alongside a proposal to the Indian Air Force to establish a C-130J Super Hercules final assembly line in India -- what would be Lockheed's first such line outside the US.

Opened the Collins India Operations Center, a new 26-acre 'Factory of the Future' manufacturing site at KIADB Aerospace Park, Bengaluru, initially producing seats, lighting and cargo systems, temperature sensors, communication/navigation systems, water solutions and evacuation slides; expected to host 2,200+ employees by 2026.

Entered a long-term licensing and technology-transfer partnership with JSW Defence for a USD 90 million unmanned-aerial-systems manufacturing facility at EMC Maheshwaram, Hyderabad, to produce Shield AI's V-BAT Group 3 drone for the Indian armed forces and export; foundation stone laid 2 Dec 2025, manufacturing targeted for Q4 2026.

Disclosed plans to invest Rs 3,000 crore in India's defence sector for military-systems manufacturing, with Haryana shortlisted as one of seven potential sites nationally (no location finalised yet); disclosed by IAI's India-arm chief of staff during a meeting with Haryana's Chief Minister.

Launched ELTX, a joint venture with India's DCX Systems Limited, to develop and localise production and maintenance of high-end airborne radars and ground-based defence systems in India, as part of deepening Israel-India defence-technology transfer.

Signed four Production Transfer Agreements with Tata Advanced Systems Limited to manufacture Rafale fighter-jet fuselage sections (lateral shells, rear/central/front sections) at a new plant in Hyderabad -- the first-ever Rafale fuselage production outside France -- with production starting FY2028 at up to two complete fuselages per month.

Established a fully-owned Indian subsidiary with a corporate office in AeroCity, New Delhi, to build out teams across defence, commercial aviation, business aviation, services & support and urban air mobility, calling India 'a key market'; follows a Feb 2024 MoU with Mahindra Defence on the C-390 medium transport aircraft.

Struck a strategic partnership with India's Reliance Defence for large-scale ammunition manufacturing (up to 200,000 artillery shells, 10,000 tons of explosives, 2,000 tons of propellants annually) at a new Reliance-built plant in the Watad industrial area, Maharashtra; on-record CEO quote calling it 'a strong commitment to partner with India.'

findings.signal: First domestically-assembled C-295 military transport aircraft rolled out (months ahead of schedule) from the Tata Advanced Systems-Airbus final assembly line in Vadodara -- the first time a private-sector facility has produced a military aircraft in India; 40 of the 56-aircraft IAF order will be built at Vadodara through 2031, with 85%+ structural/final assembly done locally.

Reliance Defence (R-Defence) tied up with Germany-based Diehl Defence to produce next-generation terminally guided munitions (TGM) for the Indian armed forces, driving local production of the Vulcano 155mm precision-guided munition system, at a greenfield integrated ammunition and explosives facility in the Watad Industrial Area, Ratnagiri, Maharashtra (shared with a related Rheinmetall AG tie-up already in this file). Total investment across both partnerships at the Ratnagiri site is Rs 5,000 crore over five years (30% equity / 70% debt), manufacturing targeted within 18 months of the June 2025 announcement.

Announced a $500 million second-phase expansion of its Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu EV plant -- enlarging the campus to roughly 900 acres with the Tamil Nadu government allocating ~500 adjacent acres -- to add dedicated production lines for electric buses and electric two-wheelers, scaling annual capacity from 50,000 to 150,000 units; part of VinFast's broader phased ~$2 billion (Rs 16,000 crore) India commitment.

Ltd., headquartered in Gurgaon, to jointly develop and produce automotive seats/interior components for the Indian market, combining TS Tech's technology with Krishna Group's position as a major seat supplier to Maruti Suzuki.

Formed a 50:50 joint venture, NDR Hayashi Automotive India Private Limited, with listed Indian auto-parts maker NDR Auto Components (incorporated 10 Oct 2025, Rs 200 crore authorized/subscribed capital, NDR investing Rs 100 crore for its 50% stake) to manufacture automotive interior components -- ambient lighting systems, carpets, dashboard inner parts, rear shades and tonneau covers -- for OEMs in India and export markets.

Combined Rs 8,000 crore investment underpinning Kia's second India manufacturing facility (300-acre site in Anantapur, Andhra Pradesh), adding 300,000 units/year of capacity alongside the existing Penukonda plant (600,000 units/year combined), including a dedicated EV production line on Kia's E-GMP platform and battery-pack assembly, to build India's first locally-produced Kia EV (compact SUV, launching late 2026); roughly 40% of output earmarked for export to the Middle East, Africa, Latin America and ASEAN.

Formed a 50:50 joint venture with India's TSF Group (Brakes India and Wheels India), registered office in Chennai, to develop and manufacture advanced electronically-controlled air systems (air compression, processing and suspension) for commercial vehicles -- described by Bosch leadership as expansion into new 'white space' segments as part of a shift from selling individual components to offering the full commercial-vehicle mobility tech stack in India; operations targeted to be fully functional by end of 2026.

findings.signal: Signed a joint venture agreement (50:50) with JSW Steel to build a greenfield 6 MTPA blast-furnace-based integrated steel plant (ironmaking through cold rolling/galvanizing) in Odisha; targeting completion by 2031 after a 48-month construction period. Builds on an October 2024 MoU and July 2025 Heads of Agreement.

Agreed to invest INR 157.5 billion (~JPY 270 billion) for a 50% stake in a new 50:50 joint venture with JSW Steel that will take over the Bhushan Power & Steel integrated steelworks in Sambalpur, Odisha (currently 4.5 MTPA of coils/sheets/bars/wire rods), with plans to expand capacity to 10 MTPA by 2030 and eventually 15 MTPA.

Committed (with 50:50 JV partner JSW Steel) approximately JPY 120 billion (JPY 99bn capex + JPY 21bn working capital; ~JPY 290bn total commitment including prior investment) to expand electrical/CRGO steel capacity at JSW JFE Electrical Steel Private Limited (Vijayanagar, Karnataka, doubling to 100,000 tpy by 2027) and JSW JFE Electrical Steel Nashik Private Limited (Nashik, Maharashtra, fivefold increase to 250,000 tpy by 2028-2030), explicitly to become the No.1 electrical steel supplier in India. The Nashik facility was formed via JFE/JSW's January 2025 acquisition of thyssenkrupp Electrical Steel India's plant there.

findings.signal: Through their 60:40 (ArcelorMittal:Nippon Steel) joint venture AM/NS India, acquired ~890 hectares in Rajayyapeta, Anakapalli district, Andhra Pradesh for a new greenfield integrated steel mill (initially sized ~7 MTPA); broke ground on March 24, 2026 for a first phase costing Rs 70,000 crore / 8.2 MTPA (total project Rs 1,35,000 crore scaling to 18 MTPA), with commissioning targeted by December 2028. ArcelorMittal Chairman Lakshmi Mittal and CEO Aditya Mittal attended in person; PM Modi participated virtually.

Announced three new renewable-energy projects in India (solar/wind/battery storage at Amaravati, Bikaner and Bachau) totalling ~US$900 million (Rs 8,145 crore) to supply captive power to its AM/NS India joint-venture operations, aiming to meet 35% of Hazira's electricity needs by 2028 and cut ~4 million tonnes of CO2 annually.

Both companies have publicly expressed willingness to jointly build a special/alloy steel plant (3-5 MTPA, automotive-grade special steel) with India's state-owned RINL on ~3,000 hectares near NMDC's Chhattisgarh raw-material sources. As of the source article this was early-stage discussion only -- no investment figure, financing structure, or start date has been disclosed, and the article notes similar past proposals stalled over weather and raw-material supply-chain issues.
